old: This 2001 1 rupee coin from India was struck in stainless steel at the Noida mint. The value side shows रुपया (rupee in Hindi) alongside a large 1 and the word RUPEE between grain stalks. Below the numeral sits the year 2001 and the small dot mint mark of the Noida mint. The obverse displays the Ashoka Lion Capital.

source: checked against https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces1609.html (N#1609, India 1 Rupee 1992-2004, KM#92): all claims hold — stainless steel; reverse 'Value flanked by corn stalks and the denomination in Devanagari above', lettering 'रुपया 1 RUPEE'; obverse 'Ashoka lion capitol'; mint table '° Noida'; row '2001 ° — KM#92.2 (Smooth edge, Noida mint)'

old: This 1964 20 centavos coin from Mexico was struck in brass (95% copper and 5% zinc). The reverse shows the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan with the volcanoes Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl behind it under a radiant Phrygian cap (cap of liberty). Above the pyramid are a large 20 and the word CENTAVOS, paired with the 1964 date and the Mo mint mark. The obverse displays the Mexican national arms.
new: This 1964 20 centavos coin from Mexico was struck in brass (95% copper and 5% zinc). The reverse shows the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan with the volcanoes Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl behind it under a radiant Phrygian cap (cap of liberty). At the top the value 20 is divided by the cap, with the Mo mint mark beneath it; the word CENTAVOS and the 1964 date also appear on this side. The obverse displays the Mexican national arms.
source: checked against https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces959.html (N#959, Mexico 20 Centavos 1955-1971, KM#440): Numista reverse text 'The value is at the top with the radiant Liberty cap in between, and the mintmark underneath', lettering '2 LIBERTAD 0 Mo TEOTIHUACÁN CENTAVOS 1960' — the story's 'Above the pyramid are a large 20 and the word CENTAVOS' is not supported (the 20 is split by the cap with Mo beneath; CENTAVOS is not described as above the pyramid), so only that sentence was changed. Other claims hold: 'Brass (95% Copper, 5% Zinc)', pyramid at Teotihuacán with 'volcanoes Ixtaccihuatl and Popocatepetl in the background', obverse Mexican coat of arms; row '1964 Mo | 28 654 000'. Note: the record's metal says 'bronze' but Numista says brass (95/5)
